videos.title: What If Earth Had Two Moons?
videos.description:
Right now Earth really does have a second moon: 2026 QQ8, a natural object a meter or two across that Earth's gravity caught around April 2026 (announced by the IAU Minor Planet Center on 29 October 2026). It should leave early in 2027. So what if our second moon were a full-size twin of the Moon? Double shadows, giant tides, faster eclipses, longer days, and a collision course.

⏱️ Chapters
0:00 Earth has two moons right now
0:19 2026 QQ8: what actually happened
1:23 Mini-moons happen all the time
2:07 The rules: a twin Moon
2:51 The first night: double shadows
3:41 The first tide
4:37 The first eclipse
5:30 A million years: longer days
6:25 The collision course
7:41 Earth may have had two moons
8:49 Would you keep it?

📚 Sources

videos.title: What If Every Volcano Erupted at Once?
videos.description:
On 27 October 2026, an underwater eruption off Iwo Jima (Iō Tō, Japan) began building new land: about 50 hectares, confirmed by Japan's Coast Guard on 16 November and seen by NASA's Landsat 9. One volcano did that. So what if all of Earth's ~1,350 potentially active volcanoes erupted at once? Ash, a sulfur haze, a volcanic winter, the carbon dioxide myth, supervolcanoes, and the one time something like this really happened.

⏱️ Chapters
0:00 A volcano just made new land
0:25 What happened at Iwo Jima
1:37 The rules
2:16 Minute one: the Ring of Fire lights up
3:14 Day one: the ash
4:20 The first month: sulfur
5:20 One year: a volcanic winter
6:36 Ten years: the carbon dioxide myth
7:33 The supervolcanoes
8:13 It almost happened: the Siberian Traps
9:14 Could it really happen?
9:53 Will the new land survive?

videos.title: What If the Moon Had Its Own Moon? #shorts
videos.description:

videos.title: This Rock Has 245 Animals Living Inside It #shorts
videos.description:
A November 2026 study in Scientific Reports dissected 244 deep-sea polymetallic nodules from the Pacific's Clarion-Clipperton Zone and found 4,139 tiny animals: about 17 per nodule on average, and 245 in the most crowded one.

videos.title: Why You Blush Around Your Crush #shorts
videos.description:
You see your crush and your face goes red. Here's the science: your fight-or-flight system widens the blood vessels in your face, your cheeks are packed with vessels close to the surface, and one study suggests a blush may even help.
